semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: "Neurosciences" is semantically equivalent to "neurodevelopment" as both terms engage with the scientific study of the nervous system, though "neurosciences" is broader and encompasses various aspects of neural research which include development.

"Neuroscience" is semantically equivalent to "neurodevelopment" in that it involves the study of the nervous system, with a focus on understanding specific aspects such as the development and growth of neural pathways.

parent_domains.justification: "Neuroscience" is a parent domain as it covers broader areas including the development of the nervous system, biological basis of behavior, and encompasses neurodevelopment.
As a parent domain, "neurosciences" is a science that encompasses a range of subjects including neurodevelopment under its umbrella.
"Theoretical neuroscience" could be considered a parent domain as it provides underlying models and theories that can be applied to understand neurodevelopment processes.

closest_parent_domain.justification: "Neuroscience" is the closest parent domain as it directly pertains to the scientific study and exploration of the nervous system, which includes the study of neurodevelopment phenomena.

child_domains.justification: "Cognitive neuroscience" is a child domain as it is a specialized field that extends under the broader study of neural mechanisms which also includes neurodevelopment.
This domain can be considered a child domain, as it involves methods and techniques to study the development of the brain, a critical part of neurodevelopment.

closest_child_domain.justification: "Cognitive neuroscience" is the closest child domain because it specifically investigates the neural connections in the brain which evolve through developmental stages.

sibling_domains.justification: "Neuroanatomy" is a sibling domain because it involves the structure of the nervous system and relates closely to how the system develops.
"Population neuroscience" is a sibling domain as it addresses the variation and prevalence of neurological pathways in populations, which can provide insights into neurodevelopment.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: "Neuroanatomy" is the closest sibling domain as it directly examines the anatomical aspects of the nervous system which are integral to understanding neurodevelopment.

unrelated_domains.justification: "Neuroergonomics" focuses on the efficiency of the interaction between people and systems, which diverges from the developmental focus of neurodevelopment.
"Synaptic plasticity" pertains to the synaptic changes and adaptability within the neurons, not directly related to the broader developmental processes addressed in neurodevelopment.
"Neurology" is more concerned with the medical aspects and diseases of the nervous system, rather than the developmental processes involved.
"Neuro-ai" deals with the intersection of AI and neural processes, which is distinct from the biologically-focused studies of neurodevelopment.
